lesson: Today we work on one thing, sound. Sound means the consonants and vowels in the words and how they feel in your mouth when you say them aloud. The poet picks words partly for how they sound together. Listen for three spots. A leaf, a leaf, each one deciding on its own. The word leaf retits and the soft F sound keeps the line quiet. Drop by patient drop puts the hard D and P sounds close together so it sounds like small taps. Washed and waiting starts both words with a W which slows you down. This works because repeated sounds make you hear the line as a unit. Your ear catches the echo and lingers. Try this. Pick two or three words in a line that start with the same sound and place them near each other. The second time listen for how the quiet sounds build until so up breaks them with one hard word.
